history.period: Reinstalled c. 1500 AD; worship said to be much older
history.summary: Ancient lakeside temple at Nuggikeri village near Dharwad, dedicated to Hanuman as Sri Balabhima. Legend says the idol appeared in a devotee's dream and was recovered from Nuggikeri Lake; the pratishtapana (reinstallation) was done by Sri Vyasatirtha (Vyasaraja), chief saint in Sri Krishnadevaraya's court, around 1500 AD. In the 18th century a Maratha Peshwa awarded the jagir of Nuggikeri to the Nuggikeri Desai family, which still manages the temple. The moolamurti is a ~5-ft granite idol coated with vermilion; the complex has a three-tier raja gopuram facing south. NOTE: the CSV's 'Hubli' is approximate - the temple is at Nuggikeri village, ~18-20 km from Hubli and closer to Dharwad (~7 km). One low-quality source claims a Mahabharata-era installation by Janamejaya; the corroborated history is the Vyasatirtha reinstallation.

name: Nuggikeri Hanuman Temple
town_description: Nuggikeri is a village on the Hubli-Dharwad airport road, known for the ancient Sri Balabhima (Hanuman) temple on the banks of Nuggikeri Lake. It lies closer to Dharwad than to Hubli.

travel.railway: Dharwad railway station, ~7 km; Hubli Junction (UBL), ~18-20 km
travel.road: Village road off the Hubballi-Dharwad bypass, ~2 km from the bypass

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; Saturdays are crowded
visitor_information.opening_hours: Early morning to evening (exact hours not reliably published; verify)
